questions.question: You run azcopy login and then azcopy copy to upload files to a container. You are an Owner of the subscription. The copy fails with AuthorizationPermissionMismatch. What should you do?

options.text: Assign yourself the Storage Blob Data Contributor role on the storage account or container
options.why: Correct. Microsoft Entra authorization for blob data requires a data role.
AzCopy with azcopy login does not use account keys.

options.text: Run azcopy login again with the --tenant-id parameter
options.why: The sign-in succeeded. The identity lacks a data role.

options.text: Assign yourself the Contributor role on the resource group
options.why: Contributor is a management role and does not grant data access.

questions.explanation: Owner and Contributor manage the account but do not include blob data actions. Use a Storage Blob Data role or a SAS.

questions.question: A folder on a file server must be copied to a blob container every night. Only new or changed files should be transferred, and files deleted from the folder must be removed from the container. Which command should you use?

options.why: Correct. sync compares the source and destination and can remove extra files.
copy transfers every file each time and does not remove deleted files.
remove deletes data. It does not copy new files.
upload-batch uploads files but does not remove files deleted from the source.

questions.explanation: azcopy sync transfers only differences, and --delete-destination true mirrors deletions.

questions.question: Which two methods can AzCopy use to authorize access to Azure Blob Storage? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.why: Correct. Use azcopy login, a managed identity or a service principal.

options.text: A SAS token appended to the URL
options.why: Correct. The SAS grants the permissions needed.

options.text: A stored access policy name passed on the command line
options.why: A policy is referenced by a SAS token, not passed to AzCopy.

options.text: The storage account key passed with a --key parameter
options.why: AzCopy does not accept the account key directly for Blob Storage.

questions.explanation: AzCopy authorizes with Microsoft Entra ID or with SAS tokens.

questions.question: An administrator on a macOS computer needs a graphical tool to browse blobs, queues, tables and file shares, change blob tiers and generate SAS tokens. What should you recommend?

options.why: Correct. It is a free cross-platform desktop application for managing Azure Storage.
AzCopy is a command-line tool.
Data Box is a physical device for offline transfers.
File Sync caches Azure file shares on Windows Server.

questions.explanation: Storage Explorer runs on Windows, macOS and Linux and uses AzCopy for transfers.

questions.question: You need to copy all blobs from a container in storage1 to a container in storage2 by using AzCopy. The data must not pass through the computer that runs the command. What should you do?

options.text: Run azcopy copy with the source and destination container URLs, each authorized by a SAS token or Microsoft Entra ID
options.why: Correct. AzCopy performs a server-to-server copy between accounts.

options.text: Download the blobs with azcopy copy, then upload them with a second azcopy copy
options.why: This sends the data through the local computer.

options.text: Run azcopy sync from a local folder
options.why: A local folder is not the source.
Geo-redundancy copies to the paired region, not to storage2.

questions.explanation: Copies between storage accounts use server-to-server APIs, so data moves directly between the accounts.
